revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Rooftop Garden
revealWordProblem.text: The firm is designing a regular decagon-shaped rooftop garden bed. It decomposes into 10 congruent triangles from the center, each with a base of 3 feet and a height of 4 feet. The garden center charges $5 per square foot for soil and plants. What is the total cost to fill the garden bed?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: One triangle: A = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 sq ft. The decagon has 10 sides, so it has 10 triangles: 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Cost = 60 × $5 = $300.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do we find the area of a regular polygon?
conceptIntro.intro: A regular polygon has all sides and all angles equal. We can decompose it (break it apart) into equal triangles from the center, then add up their areas. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A regular polygon splits into the same number of triangles as it has sides, so total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides).

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My hexagon has 6 equal sides. Each side is 6 feet, and each center triangle has a height of 5.2 feet.
First I find one triangle: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 5.2.
I multiply: 6 × 5.2 = 31.2, then ½ × 31.2 = 15.6 square feet.
A hexagon has 6 sides, so it has 6 equal triangles.
I multiply: 6 × 15.6 = 93.6. So the total area is 93.6 square feet.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller regular pentagon: each of its 5 triangles has base 4 cm and height 3 cm.
First find one triangle: ½ × 4 × 3. What is 4 × 3? Yes, 12, and half of 12 is 6 sq cm.
A pentagon has 5 sides, so how many triangles? Yes, 5.
Multiply: 5 × 6 = 30, so the total area is 30 square centimeters.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Try the practice problems below. The hint button is right there whenever you get stuck — use it, that's smart.
Remember the key idea: A regular polygon splits into the same number of triangles as it has sides, so total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides)..

approaching.stem: A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle?
approaching.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: Identify two rectangles and find each area.
Then add the two results.
Check: 5 × 3 = ?, and 4 × 2 = ?
hints: Focus on just ONE of the 6 triangles: its base is 6 ft and its height is 5.2 ft.
One triangle uses A = ½ × b × h — don't multiply by 6 yet; that step is for the whole hexagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5.2: take half of 6 first, then multiply by 5.2. Label it in sq ft.

approaching.stem: Using the triangle from the previous question, what is the total area of the hexagonal skylight?
approaching.explanation: Total area = 6 triangles × 15.6 sq ft = 93.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: Is this a rectangle plus a triangle?
Compute each area separately.
Add them.
hints: You already found one triangle's area (15.6 sq ft) in the last question — now think about the whole hexagon.
A regular hexagon splits into 6 identical triangles, so the total is 6 copies of one triangle's area.
Multiply 15.6 × 6. (Tip: do 15 × 6, then 0.6 × 6, and combine.)

approaching.stem: A regular hexagon is split into 6 triangles, each with base 4 cm and height 3.5 cm. What is the total area?
approaching.explanation: Each triangle: ½ × 4 × 3.5 = 7 sq cm. Total: 6 × 7 = 42 sq cm.
choiceFeedback: Identify all simple shapes.
Use the right formula for each.
Sum for the composite area.
hints: Two stages hide here: first one triangle (base 4 cm, height 3.5 cm), then all 6 of them.
Use ½ × 4 × 3.5 for one triangle, then multiply that result by 6 for the hexagon.
Compute ½ × 4 = 2, then 2 × 3.5 for one triangle. Now scale up by the 6 triangles.

approaching.stem: How many triangles can you make from the center of a regular pentagon?
approaching.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so drawing lines from the center to each vertex creates 5 equal triangles.
choiceFeedback: A pentagon has 5 sides — one triangle forms per side.
Count the pentagon's sides again — one triangle each.
Too many — one triangle per side, and a pentagon has 5.
hints: 'Penta' is a clue about how many sides a pentagon has.
Drawing from the center to each corner makes exactly one triangle per side of the polygon.
Count the pentagon's sides — that count equals the number of triangles.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Find the area of one triangle

approaching.correctWork: An octagon has 8 sides, not 5. Total area = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft — multiply one triangle's area by the actual number of sides (triangles), not a random number.
hints: Look at Step 4. How many sides does an octagon actually have?
An octagon has 8 sides, so it has 8 triangles: Total = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft, not 5 × 6.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Find the area of one triangle

approaching.correctWork: The student forgot to multiply by ½ when finding the triangle's area. A = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft, so Total = 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.
hints: Look at Step 3. What is the formula for the area of a triangle?
A triangle's area is ½ × base × height, not just base × height. One triangle = ½ × 6 × 4 = 12 sq ft, so the total is 5 × 12 = 60 sq ft.

onLevel.stem: A regular hexagonal floor tile splits from its center into 6 congruent triangles, each with an area of 12 cm². What is the total area of the tile?
onLevel.explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides, so it splits into 6 equal triangles. Total = 6 × 12 = 72 cm².
choiceFeedback: Identify each simple shape.
Find the area of each.
Add them together for the total.

onLevel.stem: A regular pentagonal tile splits into 5 congruent triangles. Each triangle has a base of 4 in and a height of 6 in. What is the total area of the tile?
onLevel.explanation: One triangle = ½ × 4 × 6 = 12 in². A pentagon has 5 triangles, so total = 5 × 12 = 60 in².
choiceFeedback: What shapes do you see? Rectangle? Triangle?
Use the correct formula for each shape.
Sum the areas.

onLevel.stem: An octagon tile splits into equal triangles, each with base 6 ft and height 5 ft. How many triangles, and what is the total area?
onLevel.explanation: An octagon has 8 sides, so it splits into 8 triangles. One triangle = ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 sq ft. Total = 8 × 15 = 120 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: That's one triangle — an octagon has 8; multiply.
Check how many triangles an octagon makes — is it 6 or 8?
Recount the triangles (an octagon has 8) and multiply.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — Find the Tile Area Error

workedExample.label: Decompose the tile
workedExample.work: A regular hexagonal tile = 6 congruent triangles

workedExample.label: Find the area of one triangle

onLevel.correctWork: The student stopped after finding ONE triangle. A hexagon has 6 congruent triangles, so multiply by 6: Total = 6 × 14 = 84 sq in.
hints: Look at Step 4. The work only describes one of the six triangles in the hexagon.
Multiply one triangle's area by the number of triangles: 6 × 14 = 84 sq in.

onLevel.title: Find the Area Error
onLevel.correctWork: To find total area, multiply (not add): Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 sq m. Six equal triangles means 6 times one triangle's area.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should you use to combine 6 equal triangles?
The student added 10.75 + 6 instead of multiplying 10.75 × 6.

onLevel.prompt: A regular hexagon and a regular pentagon both have triangles with the same base (6 ft) and the same height (5 ft). Which polygon has the greater total area? Explain why the number of sides matters.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: One triangle's area is ½ × ___ × ___ = ___. The hexagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The pentagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The ___ has more area because ___.
onLevel.hint: Identify each shape; write area formula; add results.
hints: Both polygons use identical triangles (base 6 ft, height 5 ft) — only the NUMBER of triangles differs.
Find one triangle's area with ½ × 6 × 5, then multiply by 6 for the hexagon and by 5 for the pentagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5 for one triangle. Then compare 6 copies with 5 copies and explain why the counts matter.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Regular Polygons is stopping after finding the area of ONE triangle and reporting that as the total area — or adding the number of triangles instead of multiplying. Remember: total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides), not (one triangle's area) + (number of sides).

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: A regular pentagon is decomposed into 5 triangles from its center. Each triangle has a base of 7 inches and a height of 4.8 inches. What is the total area of the pentagon?
exitTicket.explanation: One triangle: A = 1/2 x 7 x 4.8 = 16.8 sq in. Total = 5 x 16.8 = 84 square inches.
choiceFeedback: That's one triangle — multiply by all 5 triangles.
You skipped the ½ — each triangle is ½ × 7 × 4.8.
Right value, wrong unit — area is square inches.
hints: Two steps hide in this problem: one triangle's area first, then all 5 triangles together.
One triangle is ½ × 7 × 4.8; the pentagon is 5 of those. Skipping either step leads to a wrong path.
Take half of 7 × 4.8 to get one triangle's area, then multiply that by the 5 triangles.
